thesis: The agent stack is converging on runtime operations — context sync (CORVUS), trajectory-aware retrieval, 184M safety classifiers — which means the moat is no longer building agents but operating them, and buyers will pay for the operator layer before they pay for another agent.
doctrine: Every research signal must land as a wiring change in an existing loop (allocator, sweep, contract) with a runtime receipt — a signal that only becomes a note is a dropped signal.
proof_artifact: Extend the portfolio allocator so `portfolio_operator_runtime`-class signals (score ≥ 8) auto-generate a candidate reallocation entry in state/business_theme_portfolio.json with an evidence pointer, instead of dying in the digest queue — plus a test proving the signal→allocation path fires.
proof_next_action: Edit scripts that consume state/ai_digest_pending.json to route pattern_id=portfolio_operator_runtime items into state/improvement_queue.json as impact:high entries with target_loop=meta, then run pytest tests/ -q and commit with receipt to #shadow-log.
public_angle: Everyone is shipping agents; almost no one is operating them. I run 112 code-enforced contracts over my own runtime and the violation trend is the product — here's what an operator layer catches that your eval suite never will.
buyer_offer: Position the paid audit as 'operator-runtime readiness': prospects running multi-agent harnesses (autodev-studio-style SDLC agents) get a failure-census showing which of their agent actions lack pre/post gates — priced as the existing audit ladder, proof sourced from Shadow's 112 live contracts and declining-violations trend.
